newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals' prices mixed on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals' prices mixed on profit-taking.

text.p: Indian nickel prices on Wednesday eased while other base metals were steady in limited activity, dealers said.
Nickel prices dropped by 200 rupees at 37,000 rupees per quintal amidst demand resistance at the higher level after a gain of 400 rupees per quintal recorded last week.
"Reports of a setback in the world market also prompted profit-taking for nickel in the local market," one broker said.

Copper was steady at 13,625 rupees per quintal, zinc at 8,000 rupees and lead at 4,150 rupees. Volumes were slow as major players were awaiting an announcement of the selling prices by state-owned producers for June.
"Most of the marketmen are expecting state-owned producers to hike selling prices for June looking at the recent upsurge in the world market," a broker added.
Tin was steady at 31,400 rupees per quintal after gaining 200 rupees last week. Aluminium was indicated at the previous level of 7,650 rupees per quintal but trading was nominal.
